title: ESDS Soars 92% in First Full Week as New-Age Tech Stocks End Mixed
excerpt: Cloud infrastructure firm ESDS quadrupled its IPO price in a week of upper circuits, while fintechs rallied on hopes of a UPI merchant discount rate during Global Fintech Fest 2026.
body:
• ESDS Software surged 91.65% in its first full week of trading to close at ₹1,716.35 on the BSE — more than four times its IPO price of ₹429 — leading all new-age tech stocks.
  • The rally continued despite the stock hitting its upper circuit in every session, with the exchange narrowing its circuit limit from 20% to 10% during the week.
  • Fintech shares rallied during Global Fintech Fest 2026 on reports that a merchant discount rate of around 40 basis points could be introduced on select UPI transactions.
  • The broader market fell for a fifth straight week, with the Sensex down 2.27% amid high crude prices, rising US bond yields, and foreign investor outflows.

New-age tech stocks delivered a mixed performance this week, but one name towered above the rest. ESDS Software emerged as the biggest gainer among India's listed new-age tech companies, surging 91.65% during its first full week of trading to close at ₹1,716.35 on the BSE — 300.1% above its IPO price of ₹429.

The enterprise cloud and AI infrastructure company made its market debut on September 4, closing its first session at ₹895.50, more than double the issue price. The rally continued through every session of the week, with the stock touching its upper circuit daily until the exchange narrowed its circuit limit from 20% to 10%. The company's market capitalization stood at around ₹20,118 crore, about $2.11 billion, at the end of the week, compared with an IPO valuation of about ₹5,028 crore.

AI infrastructure appetite

The rally underscored strong investor appetite for listed AI infrastructure plays. ESDS's ₹720 crore IPO was subscribed 135.88 times, with the qualified institutional buyer portion booked 261.51 times. Choice Institutional Equities initiated coverage with a 'Buy' rating and a price target of ₹1,550, citing the AI infrastructure opportunity and the company's $1.25 billion contract with Sharon AI. The stock crossed that target within five trading sessions.

ESDS is among the two Indian players offering a complete suite spanning GPU-as-a-Service, cloud, managed services, data center infrastructure, and software solutions. A major portion of the IPO proceeds — ₹576 crore — is earmarked for cloud computing equipment and data center infrastructure.

"Valuations look stretched on trailing numbers and require successful, rapid monetization of the AI/GPU investments and international contracts to be justified."

— Santosh Meena, Head of Research at Swastika Investmart

Analysts remain divided on how much further the rally can run. Swastika Investmart's Santosh Meena called ESDS a high-quality mid-sized infrastructure and cloud player with a credible sovereign-plus-AI narrative, but cautioned that the stock now embeds very high expectations after roughly tripling in market capitalization.

Fintechs ride MDR hopes

Shares of listed fintech companies rallied during the week of Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026, with the possibility of a merchant discount rate being introduced on certain UPI transactions providing a potential earnings trigger. A report suggested an MDR of around 40 basis points could be introduced on UPI transactions involving larger merchants or higher transaction values.

Pine Labs was among the biggest beneficiaries, gaining 14.17% during the week to close at ₹202.35 — including a 16.9% jump in a single session. Paytm, MobiKwik, and AvenuesAI also posted sharp gains. UPI currently operates under a zero-MDR regime, which limits the direct revenue banks and payment companies earn from such transactions. Introducing MDR, even on a limited set, would create a direct revenue stream for banks, acquiring entities, and third-party application providers. Brokerage Bernstein named Paytm its top fintech pick, citing possible MDR introduction, growth in merchant lending, and improving operating leverage.

The developments coincided with GFF 2026, where Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for expanding UPI's international footprint and linking it with more global payment systems, while NPCI unveiled initiatives spanning ticketing, contactless payments, and international RuPay credit card payments through UPI.

Broader market under pressure

Of the 63 listed new-age tech stocks under Inc42's coverage, 33 declined between 0.01% and nearly 14% this week, while 30 ended in the green. NSE SME-listed Yudiz Solutions led the losers for the second consecutive week, falling 13.91% to ₹22.60, followed by recently listed logistics company LEAP India, which declined 9.23% to ₹144.55. LEAP India, FirstCry, Capillary Technologies, EaseMyTrip, and IndiaMART InterMESH all fell to new lows during the week. On the positive side, Lenskart, Paytm, and Nykaa touched fresh highs, while Swiggy, Honasa Consumer, and Groww registered healthy gains.

Pernia's Pop-Up Shop parent Purple Style Labs became the 64th new-age tech company under coverage after debuting on Monday, September 7. The stock listed at a discount of about 6% on the BSE but recovered to close at ₹570.15, around 0.8% below its IPO price of ₹575. The combined market capitalization of the 64 companies stood at $171.6 billion at week's end.

India's benchmark indices ended lower for the fifth consecutive week. The Sensex declined 2.27% to 74,781.76 while the Nifty 50 fell 2.09% to 23,398.10, amid elevated crude oil prices, rising global bond yields, and concerns over US inflation. Brent briefly crossed $110 per barrel before ending the week at $104.61, up 8.7%, amid the escalating US-Iran conflict. The US 10-year Treasury yield moved closer to 5%, and foreign portfolio investors pulled around ₹7,443 crore from Indian equities in the first week of September.

Other key developments

RentoMojo's IPO closed with 72.88 times subscription, with shares tentatively scheduled to list on September 17. Shiprocket's consolidated net loss narrowed 24% year-on-year to ₹13.7 crore in Q1 FY27 while operating revenue jumped 34% to ₹592.1 crore. EaseMyTrip co-founder and chairman Nishant Pitti pledged 34.51 crore shares worth around ₹211.9 crore to Motilal Oswal Financial Services for "personal use," taking his total encumbered holding to 11.26% of the company's share capital.

Swiggy agreed to sell its retail distribution platform LYNK to Udaan through a share-swap valued at around ₹500 crore, receiving a roughly 2.8% stake in the B2B ecommerce company plus an additional investment of ₹75 crore. BSE SME-listed fintech SaaS firm Veefin Solutions submitted an information memorandum to migrate to the mainboard. Ecommerce major Meesho discontinued its chief product officer role, Go Digit independent director Giridhar Aramane resigned, and BlackBuck's board approved a new wholly owned subsidiary for trucking and logistics services.

What's next

Despite near-term volatility, brokerages remain constructive on India's longer-term prospects. Morgan Stanley expects the Sensex to reach 89,000 by June 2027 provided crude oil prices moderate, while Jefferies sees opportunities emerging from India's next industrial cycle across manufacturing, semiconductors, electronics, space, and data center infrastructure. Investors will now track the US Federal Reserve's policy decision, domestic inflation data, crude oil prices, and developments in the US-Iran conflict for further cues.
